comments.author: egonosz
comments.body:
The games are mostly called slop if they are low effort.

This is low effort, without anything creative in it. It not even looks fun at all.

Yes the bar is way higher now and the reason is, because of “games” like that. Games which has zero vision (design or art) and they are literally just smashed together features from other games.

I tried some of these quick AI games, it is super funny how bad they are. They (sometimes, not in this case), look right, but after you start to play them you find out there is actually no game.

Many of the people who make games here, have no understanding about players, player value, immersion, player archetypes or anything and they just cosplay game developers. I seen it so many times, someone makes an utterly bad game and after people tell it to them and the person just blames it on anti ai people…

The problem is not the anti ai people, but the missing knowledge of that person about how to make games. If someone wants to improve, they can read learn and understand their target audience, blaming others will never help you make better game.

I do not agree with you about “we become less valuable” and the “game looks fine”. I could make a long list about what looks not fine in that game, but it is not worth it. However, the expertise will not go away because someone can prompt an AI to make a slop game. Everyone who uses AI as professional game developer, very well knows the expertise are highly needed. 

Most games what people call AI slop is AI slop, because 90% decisions are made by AI. So 90% of your game is generic or the shortest path(aka. Shortest implementation).

comments.author: According-Bake6477
comments.body: Thanks bruh, I wanted to make a survival rpg because those are the types of games I play most often. I first wrote a story where a giant werewolf attacks a town and everyone runs and hides. You being new to the town have no idea what is going on so you run and try fighting the werewolf only to be eaten over and over again. Staying in town so often you have to have fun with the villagers around you and get to know them. Eventually on top of your house you can build scorpions etc to try to kill the werewolf. Or you can get your magic / ranger skills high enough to kill the werewolf. But if you do kill the werewolf…. There might be a tragedy in there \**spoiler alert*\*. So the core story and gameplay was that. But then I just kept going by adding a dungeon and its boss. A castle with its bosses and if you beat them you take ownership of the castle. A village in the sky you can only get to if you evolve your dragon soul mate. I am not done, I still want a ton more games in the village and other puzzles.

comments.author: YaBoiSunblock
comments.body:
Creature, meet a thing called constructive criticism. If "anyone can make a game" like they're selling this stuff, then the quality bar must raise too. Nearly every "game" generated by someone using AI is an imitation of a game they liked (or a combination). They lack the requisite knowledge to do anything novel or actually cool, or make a coherent game loop. 

But I'll be fair and say that it's totally fine to experiment and build things, especially if it leads you to learning game design. It's fun. I get it. But "aigamedev" is still game dev. The novelty of most things shown is "look what a dumbass like me could do" and not "this is a cool-ass game in and of itself!"
